# The Editorial / Thought Leader

Category: `professional` · Audience: Engineering managers, writers, researchers, and architects · Output: static HTML/CSS/JS

A warm, literary portfolio where considered writing, narrative case studies, and a clear point of view lead the conversation.

A narrow reading column with a serif narrative, numbered case-study essays, dated publications, an understated CV, and a letter-like contact close.

## Default content and order

Hero → About → Writing → Projects → Experience → Skills → Contact

All identities, organizations, metrics, and work below are fictional examples. Links use example.com. The default footer labels them as illustrative; replace them before removing that label in Theme controls.

### 1. Hero — Better questions. More thoughtful systems.

Eyebrow: Mara Chen / Engineering leader & writer

Subtitle: Notes on software, teams, and the decisions between them.

I help teams find the useful question inside a complicated problem — and build the judgment, architecture, and working habits to answer it well.

CTA: [Start a conversation](mailto:mara@example.com)

### 2. About — A little context.

Subtitle: Engineering is a practice of paying attention.

Early in my career, I thought the hardest part of software was choosing the right technology. A decade of building products and leading teams taught me to look closer: Who needs this? What are we assuming? What will be difficult to change?

Today I work with organizations navigating technical and human complexity. I write down decisions, make tradeoffs visible, and create space for the people closest to a problem to shape the answer. The work is part architecture, part research, and a great deal of listening.

### 4. Projects — Selected deep dives.

The question, the constraints, and what changed.

- **Making a platform team a useful internal product** — Case study · Platform strategy · 2025–2026
  A growing engineering organization had a platform team, a roadmap, and very few repeat users. I led interviews with six product teams, mapped the recurring friction, and reframed the platform around a small set of dependable journeys. The result was a paved path teams could adopt incrementally, with ownership and feedback built into the operating model.
  Stack: Discovery · Developer experience · Operating models
  Link: https://example.com/cases/platform-as-product
- **A migration that left room to learn** — Case study · Systems architecture · 2024
  Rather than replace an aging service in one launch, we identified a seam, established a reversible routing layer, and moved one workflow at a time. This essay covers the decision record, the experiment that changed our plan, and why a clear rollback story mattered more than a perfect target diagram.
  Stack: Architecture · Risk · Incremental delivery
  Link: https://example.com/cases/reversible-migration
